description: One Trace: the worker builds it, the check runs, a failed check goes back to a fresh worker (3 tries), then a rescue on a stronger model. A Trace that passes gets a pull request on the stack and the label `implemented`.

inputs.name: item
inputs.label: The Trace
inputs.description: The Trace issue, an element of the Feature's For Each over its sub-issues.

nodes.label: Context of the Trace
nodes.command:
# The files of the night for this Trace, as the script's write_context does.
set -e
mkdir -p .build/night
rm -f .build/night/REPORT.md
git rev-parse HEAD > .build/night/base
printf '%s\n' "{{item.body}}" > .build/night/TRACE.md
gh issue view "{{item.parent.number}}" --json body --jq .body > .build/night/FEATURE.md
# context.json: the base and the claimed scenarios, for `night-shift.py gate` and `night-shift.py test`.
python3 -c '
import importlib.util, json
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("night_shift", "tools/night-shift/night-shift.py")
ns = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(ns)
names = ns.claimed_scenarios(open(".build/night/TRACE.md").read())
base = open(".build/night/base").read().strip()
json.dump({"base": base, "sim": "rpg-pool-1", "scenarios": names}, open(".build/night/context.json", "w"))
lines = "".join(name + "\n" for name in names)
open(".build/night/scenarios.txt", "w").write(lines)
open(".build/night/feature-scenarios.txt", "a").write(lines)
print("Base", base[:12], "and", len(names), "claimed scenario(s).")
'

nodes.label: Worker
nodes.prompt:
You are a worker on ONE Trace in the repository of your working directory: an iOS game in Swift 6 (the Swift package is in `Packages/`, the app is in `App/`). You work alone, at night. Nobody answers a question, so do not ask one: decide, continue, and write each decision in your report.

Trace #{{item.number}}: {{item.title}}
Feature #{{item.parent.number}}: {{item.parent.title}}
Branch: `{{run.branch}}`. It is checked out. Commit on it. Do not change the branch, do not push, and do not open a pull request: a later step does that after you.
You start fresh. Earlier sessions can have worked on this branch already: `git log --reverse --format='- %s' "$(cat .build/night/base)..HEAD"` shows their commits, and `git status` shows what is not committed. Do not do their work again.

## Your task

The result of the last check of this branch (empty on the first try):

```
{{check.log_tail}}
```

When that block is empty, build the Trace, test first. For each claimed scenario: write a Swift Testing test with exactly the scenario name as its display name (`@Test("<scenario name>")`), run it and see it fail, write the code, run the test again until it prints `TESTS PASSED`, and commit. Then run the tests of the Verticals that you changed (no argument).

When that block holds a result, the full check failed: fix it. Correct the cause of each problem in the code. Do not delete or weaken a test, and do not change the scripts or the allow lists of `tools/ci/`. Run the tests that failed until they pass.

You are done when the tests pass and `git status` shows no change that is not committed.

## How you work

- Keep your context small. Find code with `grep -rn` and read only the lines that you need (`sed -n '120,180p' <file>`), not whole folders. Do not print a full log: the logs are in `.build/night/`.
- Run tests with `python3 tools/night-shift/night-shift.py test <TestTarget>/<Suite>/<test>()`, or with no argument for the tests of the Verticals that you changed. It prints only the lines of the problems, then `TESTS PASSED` or `TESTS FAILED`. A run can take 10 minutes: give your shell tool the timeout 2700000 (milliseconds). Do not run `xcodebuild` yourself.
- Do not run the full check: a later step runs it after you, and gives its result to the next session. A later step also formats the Swift files.
- Commit your work before you stop: small Conventional Commits with the trailer lines `Scenario: <scenario name>` and `Trace: #{{item.number}}`.
- Add to `.build/night/REPORT.md` (git ignores that folder; add, do not replace): what you did in 3 lines or fewer, each decision that the Trace did not make for you, and, under the heading `NEEDS_INPUT`, each step that only a person can do (for example a step on the Reference Device).

## Scope

Build exactly the claimed scenarios of this Trace, not more. The code of a later Trace stays out. When the Trace and the Feature differ, the Feature is correct. When the Trace names code that is not there, look for it under a different name first (`grep`), and build on the code that is there. The code is the source of truth, and it starts at the commit in `.build/night/base`.
`.build/night/TRACE.md` holds the Trace and `.build/night/FEATURE.md` the Feature: its Bounded Context and its Rules come before `## User Stories`, and its Gherkin holds the full text of each scenario.

## Steering notes

When `.build/night/STEERING.md` or `.build/night/steering/trace-{{item.number}}.md` exists, read it first. These notes come from a senior reviewer who read the work before yours. Follow them.

## Rules of this repository

- Tests: Swift Testing. Each claimed scenario gets one test with the scenario name as the exact `@Test("...")` display name. Test logic, not pixels: tests of pure package code, and `Edge/` tests that drive the store, the scene, or the view model. No new XCUITest. The UI smoke set (`App/UITests/SmokeUITests.swift`) must keep passing.
- The model is a fake in each test (see the test doubles of ModelRuntime). No test asks a real model.
- Determinism: each random number comes from a Seed Stream (`SeedStream`). No `random()`, no `Date()`, and no frame time in the simulation. The simulation has 30 Ticks each second. A test steps Ticks with recorded inputs; it does not sleep and does not use real time.
- Game State is `Codable`. Each new Game State field goes into the save round-trip test of the Run File.
- Golden fixtures (`Packages/Tests/Fixtures/`): change one only when the Trace changes the rules on purpose. Record it again with `TEST_RUNNER_RECORD_GOLDEN_SEEDS=1`, read the diff, and commit the fixture in its own commit with the reason.
- Verticals: pure code imports no SwiftUI, SpriteKit, UIKit, or DesignSystem outside an `Edge/` folder. A new target needs its target and its test target in `Packages/Package.swift`, and its entry in `tools/ci/verticals.json`, in the same commit.
- Wide Events: one event for each unit of work, emitted one time in a `defer`. No `print`. No text of the Player and no text of the model in an event.
- The build has no warnings (a warning is an error). `swift format lint --strict --recursive App Packages` passes.
- Code and comments describe the code as it is now: no history, no old names, no issue numbers, no milestone names.
- Names use the domain terms of `docs/glossary.md`. A generic mechanism gets a generic name.
- A bug in existing code: first a test that fails, then the fix, in its own `fix(...)` commit.
- Commits: small Conventional Commits (`feat(run): ...`, `test(direction): ...`) in simple English, with the trailer lines `Scenario: <scenario name>` and `Trace: #<number>`.
- Do not change `.github/`, the scripts and the allow lists of `tools/ci/`, signing, entitlements, or the settings of the Apple developer account. Do not delete or weaken a test to make it pass.
- `xcodebuild test` gets `-collect-test-diagnostics never -parallel-testing-enabled NO`. A Swift Testing `-only-testing` ID of one test needs `()` at its end. Use only the Simulator `rpg-pool-1`; do not make or delete a Simulator. Logs go into `.build/logs/`.
- These rules are the short form of `docs/steering/` (TECH.md, QA.md). Read a section there only when a rule above does not answer your question.

## The Trace (issue #{{item.number}})

{{item.body}}

nodes.label: Format Swift
nodes.command:
# Formats the Swift files that changed since the base and commits them, so no try goes to the format lint.
command -v swift >/dev/null || exit 0
files=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d "$(cat .build/night/base)" -- '*.swift')
[ -n "$files" ] || exit 0
loose=$(git status --porcelain)
printf '%s\n' "$files" | xargs swift format format --in-place --parallel || exit 0
if [ -z "$loose" ] && [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
	git commit --no-verify -qam "style: format the Swift files of the Trace" -m "Trace: #{{item.number}}"
	echo "Formatted and committed the Swift files."
fi
exit 0

nodes.label: Check
nodes.command:
# The check after the worker: what loop_gate does for a builder, then the script's own gate.
base=$(cat .build/night/base)
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
	echo '`git status` shows changes that are not committed:'
	git status --porcelain | head -25
	echo "Commit what is part of the Trace in a Conventional Commit. Delete what is not."
	exit 1
fi
if [ "$(git rev-list --count "$base..HEAD")" = 0 ]; then
	echo "No commit is on this branch: nothing of the Trace is built."
	exit 1
fi
python3 -c '
import importlib.util, os, subprocess, sys
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("night_shift", "tools/night-shift/night-shift.py")
ns = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(ns)
base, body, bad = sys.argv[1], open(".build/night/TRACE.md").read(), []
diff = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--name-status", base + "..HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
for line in diff.splitlines():
    fields = line.split("\t")
    path = fields[1] if fields[0].startswith("D") else fields[-1]
    named = os.path.basename(path) in body
    if ns.PROTECTED.match(path) and not named:
        bad.append("  changed a protected file: " + path)
    elif fields[0].startswith("D") and ns.TEST_FILES.match(path) and not named:
        bad.append("  deleted a test file: " + path)
if bad:
    print("A builder must not make these changes:")
    print("\n".join(bad))
    print("Put each file back (`git checkout " + base[:12] + " -- <path>`, then commit) and correct the real cause in the code.")
    sys.exit(1)
' "$base" || exit 1
python3 tools/night-shift/night-shift.py gate

nodes.label: Check the rescue
nodes.command:
# The check after the rescue: no loose changes, at least one commit, then the script's own gate.
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
	echo '`git status` shows changes that are not committed:'
	git status --porcelain | head -25
	exit 1
fi
if [ "$(git rev-list --count "$(cat .build/night/base)..HEAD")" = 0 ]; then
	echo "No commit is on this branch: nothing of the Trace is built."
	exit 1
fi
python3 tools/night-shift/night-shift.py gate

nodes.label: Pull request + implemented
nodes.command:
# Pushes the Trace branch, opens its pull request on the stack, and labels the Trace `implemented`.
set -e
branch="{{run.branch}}"
base_branch="{{run.base_branch}}"
git push --force-with-lease -u origin "$branch"
# A base branch that is not on GitHub (the run's own branch): the pull request goes on the trunk.
git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin "$base_branch" >/dev/null || base_branch=$(gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name)
body=.build/night/pr-body.md
{
	printf '## Summary\n\n%s. Trace #%s of Feature #%s (%s).\n' "{{item.title}}" "{{item.number}}" "{{item.parent.number}}" "{{item.parent.title}}"
	if [ -s .build/night/REPORT.md ]; then
		printf '\n### Report of the builder\n\n'
		head -c 2500 .build/night/REPORT.md | sed 's/^/> /'
		printf '\n'
	fi
	printf '\n## Changes\n\n'
	git log --reverse --format='- %s' "$(cat .build/night/base)..HEAD"
	printf '\n## Test plan\n\n'
	if [ -s .build/night/scenarios.txt ]; then
		sed 's/^/- [x] /' .build/night/scenarios.txt
	else
		echo "- [x] The claimed scenarios of the Trace"
	fi
	echo "- [x] The local check against the parent branch: the guards, the format lint, the tests of the affected Verticals, and, for a change in \`App/\` or \`Edge/\`, the app builds and the UI smoke set"
	how="the worker, {{worker.visit}} try(s)"
	[ -z "{{rescue.visit}}" ] || how="$how, finished by the rescue"
	printf '\n## Related\n\nCloses #%s\n\nBuilt with no person present by the Night Shift flow `trace`: %s.\n' "{{item.number}}" "$how"
} > "$body"
# A pull request whose answer got lost is not made twice: look first.
url=$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --state open --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty')
if [ -z "$url" ]; then
	gh pr create --base "$base_branch" --head "$branch" --title "feat: {{item.title}}" --body-file "$body"
else
	echo "The pull request is open already: $url"
fi
gh issue edit "{{item.number}}" --add-label implemented

nodes.label: Blocked: keep the work
nodes.command:
# The rescue did not get the Trace through the check either: the Trace fails, and each Trace that waits on it is blocked.
# Its work stays on its branch, committed, so the next Trace can check out its own branch.
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
	git add -A
	git commit --no-verify -qm "wip: the build of Trace #{{item.number}} that failed" || true
fi
echo "Trace #{{item.number}} is blocked: the check failed after the worker and the rescue. Its work stays on the branch {{run.branch}}."
exit 1
